old_problem: The Procedure mixes standard Type 19 memory-array map fields with Type 3 chassis identity/status fields. The prior review left their ownership pending even though DMTF defines it. DeepSeek's header grep cannot validate address intervals, extended-address selection, Type 16 handle references or Partition Width.
disposition_reason: Resolve Pending and Source Conflict. DMTF maps Starting/Ending/Extended Addresses, Memory Array Handle and Partition Width to Type 19; every handle is reconciled to Type 16 Physical Memory Array. The listed Manufacturer/chassis identity/status/security fields form a mandatory Type 3 companion branch. Exact topology/ranges and permitted holes/interleave are Project Configuration. Complete interval, sentinel, handle and persistence checks replace the narrow grep; logs are preserved.
decision_basis: XLSX row 1936, same-row tests.json/DeepSeek, GPT V2, historical record and ED-01 through ED-30 were read; the actual next queue row was directly opened as Functionality 1937 / Wistron-BIOS-00479-V002 / 04f35a8326809db5.
DMTF field definitions determine Type 19 versus Type 3 ownership without deleting any Procedure field.
Type 19 is relational: every Memory Array Handle must resolve to Type 16 and effective address intervals must match the approved physical-array topology.
Legacy start/end values and extended fields are interpreted by the standard sentinel rules; ranges must be ordered, non-overlapping except where explicitly allowed, and cover the approved map.
One approved warm reboot requires same-target Boot ID and OS Ready; all complete structures and preserved logs are compared semantically.
No dmidecode, SSH, reboot, log-clear, firmware, SMBIOS or DUT action was performed.

test_case.test_name: SMBIOS Type 19 array-map topology, Type 16 handle and Type 3 companion persistence
test_case.purpose: Validate every Type 19 effective memory-array interval, referenced Type 16 array and Partition Width plus every listed Type 3 chassis field against the exact recipe before and after one approved warm reboot.
required_package: Exact SUT/BIOS/SMBIOS identity and versioned Type 19/Type 16 topology: record count, effective ranges, handles, partition widths, allowed gaps/overlaps and address units
Validated dmidecode and complete Type 19/16/3 parser implementing legacy-versus-extended sentinel rules and protected raw evidence
Secure access, approved warm reboot/window/Boot ID timeout and independent console/BMC recovery
Preserved platform logs and protected address/identity evidence policy
test_case.test_command: READ-ONLY COLLECTION AROUND ONE APPROVED REBOOT; DO NOT EXECUTE DURING REVIEW. Capture exact target identity and preserved logs. Securely collect complete `dmidecode --type 19`, referenced `--type 16`, and `--type 3` output with stdout/stderr/status. Normalize each Type 19 effective inclusive interval using standard legacy/extended rules, resolve its Type 16 handle, validate range order, allowed overlap/gaps and Partition Width against the recipe, and separately compare all listed Type 3 fields. After one approved OS warm reboot with Boot ID/OS Ready proof, repeat and semantic-diff all structures. No grep, log clear, secret exposure, firmware/SMBIOS mutation or retry.
test_case.expected_result: Every expected Type 19 record exists with correct effective start/end, valid referenced Type 16 handle and Partition Width; intervals match the approved array map without unapproved gaps/overlaps and use legacy/extended fields correctly. Type 3 companion fields are correct. All remain semantically stable after the same SUT returns to OS Ready.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires complete successful pre/post Type 19/16/3 collections, exact identity, all handle/range/sentinel/width/topology and chassis-field checks, approved Boot ID-changing reboot and OS Ready. FAIL on missing/extra/malformed record, unresolved handle, inverted/out-of-policy interval, wrong width, address representation error, companion mismatch or reboot/health failure. NOT READY covers missing topology/oracles/access/recovery. Header-only output cannot PASS; end user owns verdict.
safety_gate: Collection is read-only; never modify memory mapping, BIOS, SMBIOS, chassis security or firmware.
Preserve complete logs/output and protect memory addresses and identity/security fields; never clear logs or suppress errors.
Use secure verified access and approved reboot/recovery only; no plaintext secrets or disabled host verification.
Stop on wrong target, parser ambiguity, reboot failure or unexpected topology change; no automatic retry.
expected_evidence: Exact row/variant, target/BIOS/SMBIOS/dmidecode/parser identities and Type 19/16 plus Type 3 matrices
Complete pre/post Type 19/16/3 raw output/status and protected hashes
Per-record effective interval, sentinel path, Type 16 handle resolution, Partition Width and gap/overlap evaluation
Approved reboot timeline, Boot IDs, same-target OS Ready and preserved platform logs/health
No-clear/no-write/no-retry audit, workload restore and engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: On reboot failure retain first evidence and use only the approved console/BMC boot runbook. On missing handle, invalid interval or topology drift, preserve full SMBIOS tables and firmware identity, make no BIOS/memory-map change and escalate to BIOS/platform owner. Do not auto-reboot or edit data to force alignment.

source_conflict.reason: DMTF maps Type 19, referenced Type 16 and Type 3 fields exactly; all branches remain, so no owner choice or field deletion is needed.
